$comment: The published cohort definition for the Machine Readers surface. DATA, not code — no switch statements anywhere. Served verbatim at https://juanlentino.com/_sn/rights-signals/taxonomy so any number derived from it can be checked against it. See docs/MACHINE-READERS.md in signal-and-noise-tools for the full contract.

matching.note: Entries are tested in array order and the FIRST match wins, so specific tokens must precede the generic ones they contain (applebot-extended before applebot; googlebot-image before googlebot). Plain substring rather than regex on purpose: no escaping subtleties, no catastrophic backtracking on a hostile UA, and a reviewer can verify a match by eye. Tokens that risk matching inside an unrelated word carry their punctuation (curl/, axios/, java/).

purpose_vocabulary.search: Index building for a search product.
purpose_vocabulary.retrieval: Live grounding for an AI answer, agent-initiated.
purpose_vocabulary.user: User-directed single fetch, not a crawl.
purpose_vocabulary.ads: Advertising and business-product fetches: ad-safety validation and catalogue checks.
purpose_vocabulary.unknown: Unclassified, or a documented agent whose declared purpose has no home in this vocabulary yet.

field_contract.match: Lowercase token matched as a substring against the lowercased User-Agent.
field_contract.vendor: Owning organisation, or null where not identifiable. Independent of purpose.
field_contract.purpose: One value from purpose_vocabulary. Reflects the operator's OWN declared function, not our inference about downstream use.
field_contract.source: URL of the vendor's own published declaration, or null where no first-party page exists.
field_contract.declared: true when purpose comes from the vendor's own published page; false when it rests on third-party reporting. A surface whose claim is 'observed vs declared' must not blur the two.
field_contract.training_corpus_source: true when content collected by this agent is known to feed AI training corpora, REGARDLESS of purpose. Keeps the dual role queryable without overloading purpose.
field_contract.observable: false for tokens that never appear in a request (robots.txt control tokens). Any observed hit on these is spoofed or synthetic.
field_contract.no_user_agent: true when the vendor documents the token as a robots.txt control token with no HTTP user agent of its own (taxonomy 1.4.0). The vendor never sends it, so a request presenting it is impersonation, and a reader should count the hit under this entry's id as never the vendor. Present only with observable false; the sensor records the entry id as agent.
field_contract.cf_verified: true when the agent is listed in Cloudflare's public verified-bots directory (Radar bots directory; taxonomy 1.5.0), so Cloudflare sets its verified-bot category on a genuine request from it. A hit claiming this agent that Cloudflare did NOT verify, on a day the sensor recorded verification, is an impostor: counted, never credited. Absent reads as false, and false never reclassifies a hit. Never on an entry with observable false. The read path stamps it on every aggregate row from the row's agent id.
field_contract.ip_ranges_url: The vendor's own published list of the IP ranges its crawler uses (taxonomy 1.6.0), fetched at most daily. The sensor checks the client IP of a request claiming this agent against it and records only the answer as vendor_verified (blob16): '1' in range, '0' list read and out of range, '' not measured. An out-of-range IP alone is not an impostor (vendor lists are incomplete); a reader needs a second signal. No IP is stored.
field_contract.home_networks: Lowercase substrings of cf.asOrganization the vendor's crawler is known to run from (taxonomy 1.6.0). The read path stamps home_network on each aggregate row: '1' the row's network matches one, '0' it matches none, '' the agent has no list or the network was not measured. Off a home network AND unverified reads as an impostor to the plugin; '' never reclassifies.
field_contract.note: Present only where the call is contested or the vendor's declaration is internally mixed.
field_contract.first_party: true when the request comes from this site's own tooling. Self-traffic is not readership and headline totals exclude it. Identified from Workers Logs, not guessed.

entries.note: FIRST-PARTY. The hourly live probe in the THEME repo's smoke-test.yml. At taxonomy time it was the single largest reader of the rights surfaces (330 of ~630 rights reads over 7 days), which is the site checking itself, not readership.
FIRST-PARTY. scripts/check-rights-signals.mjs, the Worker's own post-deploy gate. Second-largest rights reader. Not matched by any frozen family, so it recorded nothing at all before v1.12.0.
FIRST-PARTY. The plugin's rights-anchor-check and rights-drift-check health probes, which carry the plugin version in the token.
FIRST-PARTY. The plugin's provenance integrity checker.

FIRST-PARTY. The provenance worker's hourly capture of the rights files for the ledger (sn-provenance 1.21.1 names itself; before that its three reads an hour filed as unclassified-machine and were 468 of the last 500 rows of the rights stream on 2026-09-19).
FIRST-PARTY. The provenance ledger verifier.
OpenAI: 'used to surface websites in search results in ChatGPT's search features'. Distinct from GPTBot and NOT a training crawler.
User-directed. OpenAI states robots.txt training rules may not apply because a person asked for this specific fetch. MUST NOT be counted as train.

OpenAI: validates 'the safety of web pages submitted as ads on ChatGPT', and explicitly does not train generative models. Filed under the 'ads' purpose added in taxonomy 1.1.0 rather than stretched into 'security', which would have implied a scanner.

Anthropic: 'navigates the web to improve search result quality for users'. Falls to family other-bot under the frozen v1.4.0 family regex, which never matched this token — the vendor axis is what makes it visible.
User-directed. MUST NOT be counted as train.
Legacy token carried by the frozen family regex. Not present in Anthropic's current documentation; retained so historical family rows keep a vendor.

Control token, like Applebot-Extended: Google documents it as the way to 'manage whether content may be used for training future generations of Gemini models', not as a fetching agent. Expect ~0 observed hits. Taxonomy 1.4.0: Google states 'Google-Extended doesn't have a separate HTTP request user agent string' (https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers), so a request presenting it is never Google.

CONTESTED FILING. Google: 'crawls requested by site owners for building Vertex AI Agents'. Filed retrieval because it builds grounding corpora that serve AI answers rather than foundation-model weights; a reasonable reader could argue train.
Search Console's Rich Result Test and URL inspection — owner-triggered SEO tooling, not a crawl.

CORRECTS A LIVE OVER-COUNT. Google documents GoogleOther as a 'generic crawler that may be used by various product teams for fetching publicly accessible content' — it is not AI-specific. The frozen family regex files it as google-ai, which sits inside the published AI-training set, so generic Google fetches are currently reported as AI-training reads. family is frozen and stays wrong; purpose is what should be read. Re-checked for taxonomy 1.4.0 (2026-10-11, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers): Google adds that it may be used for one-off crawls for internal research and development, and that its robots.txt rules affect no specific product. No value in purpose_vocabulary names generic product-team or research fetching, and unknown is defined to cover a documented agent whose declared purpose has no home here, so purpose stays unknown.
Perplexity: 'not used for web crawling or to collect content for training AI foundation models'.
Perplexity: 'designed to surface and link websites in search results', and 'not used to crawl content for AI foundation models'.

NOT AN OBSERVABLE AGENT. Apple: 'Applebot-Extended does not crawl webpages' — it is a robots.txt control token used only to decide how data already collected by Applebot may be used. The requested Apple train/search split cannot be measured from request logs. The frozen family apple-ai therefore reports a phantom: any non-zero count is spoofed or synthetic.
The only Apple agent that actually fetches. training_corpus_source is true because Applebot-Extended governs the training use of exactly this agent's collection.

Meta declares a mixed function: 'training foundation AI models or improving products by indexing content directly'. Filed train because training is named first and is the reason the rights surfaces exist.
Meta: 'helping AI navigate websites to complete tasks for users' — agent-initiated grounding, not corpus collection.
Improves Meta AI search results. Invisible to the frozen family classifier, which returns null for this token — recorded only under the additive unclassified-machine family.
Meta's advertising and business products. Same class as OAI-AdsBot; see the 'ads' purpose.

Link unfurler: fetches 'title, description, and thumbnail image' for content shared into Meta apps. Returns null from the frozen family classifier (no bot/crawler/spider substring), so it has never been recorded at all.

DECIDED: archive. Common Crawl's own declaration is 'an open repository of web crawl data that is universally accessible and analyzable by anyone' — archiving, with no claim to train models. Its role as one of the largest AI training corpora is real but is a downstream fact about consumers, not the operator's declared purpose, so it rides training_corpus_source rather than overloading purpose. Filing it train would attribute to Common Crawl an intent it does not state; filing it archive alone would hide the dual role. This is the case the boolean exists for.

FOUND BY THE UNKNOWN-AGENT REVIEW, 40 minutes after the sensor went live , the first thing RULE 2 surfaced. Amazon: 'used to improve search experiences in Amazon products and services', eligible to appear in surfaces such as Alexa, and explicitly does NOT train generative models. The frozen /amazonbot/i family does not match this token, so it lands in other-bot; the vendor axis is what makes it visible.

Amazon's user-initiated fetcher, e.g. 'responding to Alexa queries that require up-to-date information'. Explicitly not used for training. Like every *-User agent it MUST NOT be counted as train. Not matched by any frozen family, so it records only under unclassified-machine.

RECLASSIFIED in taxonomy 1.2.0, on evidence found by the RULE 2 unknown-agent review. Amazon documents THREE agents on one page: Amazonbot, Amzn-SearchBot and Amzn-User. The v1.0.0 filing of `search` rested on Amazon leading with 'improve our products and services' while hedging training as 'may be used'. That reading does not survive a dedicated Amzn-SearchBot existing: with search and user-directed fetching carved into their own agents, the only AI purpose Amazonbot still declares is model training. Filing it `search` would double-book a purpose Amazon assigns elsewhere and hide the training signal, which is the one the rights claim turns on.

NO FIRST-PARTY DECLARATION EXISTS. ByteDance publishes no crawler page comparable to OpenAI's or Anthropic's; the training purpose rests on third-party reporting only. declared=false is the honest record of that, and this surface must not present an inference as a declaration.

CORRECTS A LIVE OVER-COUNT. Mistral: 'indexing purposes only', explicitly 'not used for generative AI training'. The frozen family regex /mistralai/i files all three Mistral agents as the mistral family, which sits inside the published AI-training set.
User-directed; Mistral states it is not used for generative AI training. Same over-count as mistralai-index.

CORRECTED in taxonomy 1.1.0, re-checked for 1.4.0 (2026-10-11). Cohere now publishes a crawler page, but it does not name the cohere-ai token: it says Cohere does not use bots or user agents to crawl web content for training generative AI models 'at this time', and its table of bots is empty. The best available third-party record (Known Agents, formerly Dark Visitors) still calls cohere-ai an unconfirmed, undocumented agent, 'possibly' dispatched by Cohere's chat products in response to user prompts. One directory's 'possibly' is not a declaration, so purpose stays unknown and declared stays false. training_corpus_source is false: Cohere's page rules out training crawling by any bot it runs today, though it does not say this token is one of them.
Allen Institute: 'This web content is used to train open language models.'

Diffbot's agent for 'requests on behalf of individual users'. Must precede the bare diffbot token. The frozen family regex /diffbot/i files both as the diffbot family, so this is the same shape of over-count as googleother and MistralAI-Index.

Diffbot documents 'Diffbot' for general web crawling into its commercial Knowledge Graph. CONTESTED: a structured-data product is corpus collection, but not foundation-model training, and Diffbot markets the graph for AI grounding. Filed train with the boolean set. NOTE that customer-run Crawlbot crawls use a CUSTOMER-SET user agent, so they do not appear here at all.

FIRST-PARTY. This is juanlentino.com's own uptime monitor, and at taxonomy time it is the single largest bucket in the dataset (6,403 of 17,463 reads over 30d, 37%). It is the site measuring itself, not readership. first_party exists so headline totals can exclude it instead of quietly carrying it.
